item.title: A Complete Group
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A total of 49 tombs(and one vacant tomb) located underground. The bodies belonged to a group of reality benders who could 'bless' (call it what you will) chosen areas and prevent anyone within those areas from ever getting injured or killed. As of now,their corpses now 'curse' people within 20 meters of them. It was something not even they knew the reason for.

Central Narrative: The story will begin with the only known survivor of the group being discovered and interviewed in the former headquarters of the group. The survivor explains that over 23 years,they have researched and logged all areas affected by their 'blessings' in order to see where the best places to bless would be.

He further explains that the reason they have all passed away was due to the leader.(Who he refers to as "The Willow") Her death caused a chain reaction upon all the members of the group to perish,leaving only the unnamed survivor to bury them.

Hook: If you enjoy stories about the history of abandoned places,this could definitely intrigue you if I do it right. In the end,its a simple story about the past of a group of people.

Additional Notes:
•The article will include the logs and research created by their group
•In the article,the survivor will state that his curse was the inability to leave the Headquarters and the tombs.He states that "the others were not so lucky."

•If there is anything that seems off,please tell me.

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: The innate nature of things.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP is an Extradimensional space (hereafter referred to as ES). ES exists as a parallel dimension to our own. ES is filled with esoteric machines that continuously enforce the physical logical and thaumaturgic laws of reality.

Central Narrative: foundation discovers common abstract mechanism enabling magic. Through prodding it manage to open a door to ES. Finds machines and fucks with them discovering that they sustain the laws of the universe. ES has a layered structure and foundation goes deeper uncovering larger machines responsible for more significant laws. Security is tight and progress becomes harder as they get further in. As the foundation make progress, they learn that our universe is built of the foundation of one that came before. Nothing about this prior universe will ever make sense to us because it does not use any of the laws we use. The old universe ended because of a great machine that destroyed it while building another. The first great reveal is that said machine is the SCP.

The foundation find that some of the machines seem to have no effect on enforcing universal laws. A brave researcher fucks with one without permission and causes it to output a huge mass of metal. Analysis of this metal reveals some haphazard data encoded within. Foundation works out that the machine is trying to deliver a message. estimates that as much as 70% of the machine is dedicated to nothing more than composing and outputting a message. They integrate mechanical typewriters into parts of the machine and try and teach it English. After a very long time they get something coherent. The message simply reads.

“this is our gift to you.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Every law we know of both physical, logical and thaumaturgical is not innate and is instead enforced upon reality by a machine that you can physically touch. Where did the machines come from and what would happen if they were switched off?

Additional Notes:

I’m not 100% sure about all of the narrative beats here but this is the fundamental idea that I want to write. There are some fun bits that could be thrown in like logs from the foundation testing on the machines. More about the machine’s relationship with the forces of thaumaturgy could be explored. Also perhaps a GOI finds out about the machine and the foundation have to find a way to fortify it.

Could have some machines be found damaged. Suggests that others have been here and asks questions about what laws are not working the way they should. Could also have machines enforcing laws that the foundation where not aware of, creating even more intrigue.

I’d like to find a way of exploring the cosmic horror of what came before. My idea is that the previous universe was so awful that beings in that universe built the machine to create a better one, even though they could never live in it.

item.title: Lightspeed shoes
item.content:encoded:
A pair of brand-name running shoes which exponentially accelerate its wearer's speed based on the length of their stride, with strides 45 centimeters or longer plateauing at 99.9% c, due to the fact that no object with matter can achieve light speed.

Understandably, following the laws of physics, this would mean anyone wearing these shoes and attempting to walk would be sent flying at unimaginable speeds while likely destroying any object in their path while also igniting themselves and a good deal of their surroundings from the massive friction.

also, for some clarification, while I stated "strides" I would like to clarify that it applies to general movement including lifting the foot, kicking, etcetera, but it felt necessary to give some sort of measurement to reference from

item.title: Re: No Happy Endings
item.content:encoded:
I think this could be a SCP or tale easily (and yes you can make a tale about an SCP entry that doesn’t exist on the mainlist)

But to make it work as a SCP you’ll have to differentiate with a narrative beyond just the person inside saying “please help me” and give exposition dumps

Two suggestions:
1) expand the foundation’s research into this person the SCP is looking for, make that an adventure for the reader to go on

2) the ending won’t work as a stinger, in my opinion. Even if it’s really funny lyrics, the SCP complaining about being locked away just doesn’t seem to be a satisfying ending to me. I would try to think of something different.

item.title: 500 grains of people (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the collective term for 500 sapient grains of sand, which all spontaneously appeared in Memphis Tennessee. They don't need to eat or drink, but they do sleep. They move around by sliding around, via anomalous means. They can all talk, but don't have any mouths, or facial features. They're all as audible as normal human beings, and are able to be killed easily, such as by stomping, throwing, etc.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The Foundation first acquires SCP-X when reports of screams in Memphis Tennessee, coming from nowhere start coming in. The Foundation investigates, and soon find the source, approximately 500 grains of sand. They take them to a site, and get the instances to pick one grain to explain what's going on.

The grain explains that they're from the year 2025, and during that year, several ginormous extraterrestrial space crafts landed on earth, and started killing every human they could find. Not animals, they left horses, dogs, everything else alone. They didn't offer surrender to the humans either.

When cities were clear of humans, the aliens started moving in to the houses, and started taking on the humans lives. Except they lacked all the problems that humans had. There weren't wars between them, they were eco friendly, using resources such as solar panels and energy supplies they had brought to earth from their ships. (The grain of sand knows this because he used to be a part of a group of humans who snuck into cities and tried to reclaim them.)

The aliens also seemed to have highly advanced technology, such as weapons that could freeze people in place, and even time machines. Eventually, almost the entire human population was wiped out. And soon the aliens began hording the last humans into chamber, where they were either vaporized, or transformed into other entities, such as animals, or plants, and even furniture. The grain of sand (who was a human at the time) was horded into a large chamber with around 500 other people. The SCP-X instance realized that the aliens operating the machine appeared to be panicking, and the machine malfunctioned, turning the 500 people into grains of sand instead of animals or furniture. It then started a countdown, and apparently went into a kind of "time travel mode", and sent them into the past.

The grains of sand all show signs of traumatization, reasonably. The file is then updated in February of 2025, stating that several ginormous extraterrestrial space crafts appeared out of a wormhole in the Earths solar system. Using information gathered from the SCP-X instances, the Foundation neutralizes the threat.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber here is the end of the world vibe the story brings about, and how there were so little survivors.

Additional Notes: This is a little idea I came up with, let me know what you think of it, I'm open to all criticism and am looking to improve!

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the wonderful world of 400 or less ;-). Read: There is plenty of Foundation involvement and a lot of the plot holes have been covered. Just not in the version presented due to space limits.

1) It's a fairly stout backpack. Definitely worth the $10 in a second-hand store. And that assumes someone doesn't keep it for themselves when they find it. Also, as the body evaporates, there's no crime scene; that also gives it the appearance of an abandoned backpack after a death. As Page rarely dies in a secluded area, it's usually not long before someone finds it.

2) The Foundation had it for a while, but it was "released" when it was grabbed in a GOC raid. One raider kept it just a little too long. The Foundation tries to grab it when it pops up, and a couple of Foundation agents have been lost to the backpack because they ignored parts of the containment process. Thus. while it's easy to track via the IP address of wherever Page logs in, they can't always send someone to retrieve it, especially as they need to do so in less than an hour.

The backpack always creates debates with site admins: Keep in mind that it represents a being with 50 years of life experience who has acquired a wide variety of skills.

3) I'm already looking into the Tales….

SCP-5156 is a six foot tall humanoid entity with completely white eyes, a black body, and a crown.

SCP-5156 is able to merge with anything by going into the brain and controlling the person from the inside, this rarely happens.

Deleted at -21 and four votes.

Feedback Ported:

7ballcraze

+ show block
– hide block

So let's start

SCP-5156 is to be kept in a 1767.84 centimeters wide cell with special NORA security cameras and iron doors due to SCP-5156's exceptional strength.

What. 1767.84 centimeters? Why so specific? If the cell is 1767.85 will it die? This is a common problem with SCPs (heck I've done it a few times before), you don't need to specify the lengths of the cell. You can just say "SCP-XXXX is to be contained in a humanoid cell."

SCP-5156 is a six foot tall humanoid that looks roughly like a king with white eyes.

Huh? Looks roughly? Weird. Also looking like a king could mean anything. It could be an Egyptian king or a British king etc. You can just say "SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature that wears a crown (or whatever it is wearing). SCP-XXXX's eyes are completely white as well."

SCP-5156 is able to merge with anything granting it the body and/or powers due to it's virus.

Ok first off, the footnote could have easily been in the paragraph. Think of footnotes like parentheses. Next, what do you mean by merge with anything? Does it do a body snatcher and replicate them? Or is it like the Thing where it kill and replaces the person. Also what's "it's virus"?

SCP-5156 can speak english, spanish, and french. SCP-5156 is very intelligent and is able to learn very quickly.

I believe the words English, Spanish, and French should be uppercase. Also this is kind of bland to be honest. Like cool it's very smart, it's never brought up again. It just feels like a X-man architype.

SCP-5156 can't attack the person they morph into due to being in the body and if the body SCP-5156 is in gets destroyed so does SCP-5156.

How do they know that? Did SCP-5156 tell them? I guess this is the only "downside" it has. Think of humanoid SCPs as something great (seeing into the future) with unsuspecting consequences (you can't look at food because it will look like feces). That's what made SCP-187 a good SCP since it's a monkey's paw effect. I suggest you also look into more modern humanoid SCPs since SCP-187 is kind of old (but still not terrible).

SCP-5156 was first discovered on 11/██/███ in a factory at ██████ and was found by J████ B████ during a security search at the █████ factory. SCP-5156 was trying to attack J████ B████ due to unknows reasons. SCP-5156 was in a 6 foot box when found for unknown reasons.

Uh, I feel like it was redacted a little too much. I want to at least know the mysterious JB's first name. Also, the factory could've been named to give the SCP more life and interest. Since you would want to know more about the factory. Also did the month have to be blocked out in the date? It seems really silly.

██████: Hello SCP-5156 today you are here so we can find out why you were in a box got it?

Commas can sometimes be annoying but in conversations it can act as a break in a sentence. If I read this sentence out loud then it would be a mouthful. The way I'd put it is "Hello SCP-5156, we have some questions we want to ask."

well I fell out of her body and into the box everybody said I was too dangerous and just kept me in there with the lid closed.

First, well should be capitalized since it was the first word in a sentence. Second, how strong is that box? Earlier you said they had to get iron doors (I think the SCP sites do have iron doors on all SCP cells though) and this smart guy gets trapped in a box? This is also after everyone said he was too dangerous.

After the interview SCP-5156 was taken back to it's cell and the research team started to see if they could get more information about █████████ ██████████ no progress has been achieved.

It's means it is. Its is for referring to objects that posses something. For example, its got a minifridge.

Subject: D-34734
Time: June 27th 4:43 PM EST

The Subject and Time have to be bolded.

Result: SCP-5156 went into D-34734's body as planned and started causing chaos. While the chaos happened a guard removed SCP-5156 from D-34734's body

What kind of chaos? Just saying causing chaos makes the reader less interested in the story.

Analysis: SCP-5156 can cause chaos inside a body but it it very easy to stop.

First you said it was dangerous, and now it's just easy to stop? This is a bit confusing. I suggest going to the forums for help on making your SCP.

As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

SCP-5215 is a remote village named "Kaisariana" approximately ████ km south of the ████ border. At a first inspection, it looks like an ordinary village but when closer at about 100 meters from the entrance the subject enters a different dimension. In said dimension the subject(s) enter a comatose state for about 20-30 minutes, upon waking up observations show very light memory loss only including the last 12 hours of their life. Once awoken subjects are in a recovering state and can barely move. Once recovered their brain thinks that they were in this situation beforehand and were injured due to memory loss. Some of these "situations" are the following: World war 1 and 2, the Vietnam war, the cold war, the Afghanistan invasion, Iraq, etc. These anomalous events only occur under circumstances that are not yet known. The SCP-5215 population is around 70 people which are to be labeled SCP5215-2. Said subjects usually pass the age of 60 but all of them show advanced metabolism, motor skills, and huge life spans reaching up to 300000. Three of these inhabitants however retain abilities that can potentially cause a lot of damage should a total containment failure occur, therefore they are to be labeled SCP-5215-1 instances (check addendum 5215-A B and C). However, these SCP-5215-1 instances show to be more advanced at everything and potentially be immortal. Said instance is extremely hard to contain due to it being extremely resistant to most forms of physical damage, very intelligent, and immune to the effects of every other SCP.
